data.narrative:
ClearSpace, a Series A+ Space & Aerospace company founded by Luc Piguet and Muriel Richard, has raised $36M to date. The valuation universe consists of 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs. This represents a nascent sector with limited comparable transaction data.

Standard triangulation methods face material constraints. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent stage, or comparable valuation tier yields fewer than 3 datapoints, rendering sector-wide medians unreliable proxies. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the Space & Aerospace median stands at 24.6x across the 6 public tickers—cannot be applied because ClearSpace's revenue is not disclosed, a typical limitation for private companies.

The absence of usable quantitative triangulation methods reflects structural constraints in frontier aerospace rather than analytical failure. Valuation would require either: disclosure of ClearSpace's revenue run-rate to enable public-comp anchoring; identification of sufficiently similar-stage private funding rounds; or execution of scenario-based DCF analysis with disclosed financial guidance. Without these inputs, no defensible valuation range can be synthesized from the available data. Any assignment of value at this stage should rest explicitly on deal-specific due diligence and management discussions rather than market multiples.
